title: Make review-worker termination and lease recovery truthful
description:
`ReviewWorker` stops claiming work after SIGTERM, but executor shutdown still joins any active Hermes request. The default request timeout is 7,200 seconds while Compose grants 150 seconds, so an orchestrator normally ends a blocked process with SIGKILL. Lease fencing prevents corrupt durable state, but rollout recovery is delayed and the abandoned model call can consume work before a later retry.

Keep `ReviewWorker`, the Hermes transport, and the job lease as the existing owners. Make the termination policy truthful: either prove transport cancellation within the grace period or explicitly size and document forced termination plus lease-expiry recovery. Never release a lease early while the Hermes call can still be running.

## Steps to Reproduce

Claim a review with a Hermes client that does not return, send SIGTERM, and observe the process remain in executor shutdown beyond the 150-second container grace.

## Acceptance Criteria

Termination behavior is explicit and tested; timeout, grace, lease expiry, and recovery form one documented policy; no lease is released while model work can still run; writes remain generation-fenced.
acceptance_criteria: Termination behavior is explicit and tested against a blocked Hermes call; request timeout, stop grace, lease expiry, and recovery delay form one documented policy; no lease is released while model work can still run; durable writes remain generation-fenced.
close_reason: Worker termination now has an attempt-neutral activation boundary, saturated recovery cadence, truthful cross-platform grace, exact lease fencing, and verified operator documentation.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Canonical owners remain ReviewWorker, HermesChatClient, the durable job lease, and platform termination settings. Chosen policy: do not shorten the 7,200-second review timeout, detach active work, or expire a lease while Hermes can still run. SIGTERM stops new claims; active requests keep their heartbeats until completion or platform force-termination. Compose and OpenShift will share one configurable 150-second default grace, and operations docs will state the exact recovery bound: grace plus lease plus recovery interval (300 seconds by default from SIGTERM). Proof: a blocked Hermes-call behavior test, deployment/docs contract checks, and canonical validation. Non-goals: no cancellable HTTP rewrite, daemon executor, new service, schema change, or early lease release.

title: Reduce PostgreSQL blast radius with service-specific roles
description:
All runtime processes currently use one PostgreSQL credential even though admission, gateway, workers, publisher, and migrations have different write authority. This increases blast radius, but the pilot is a single-tenant deployment and the operational cost of multiple roles is real.

First document a concrete threat model and query/connection budget. If the reduction is material, design the smallest practical grant split with a separate migration owner and tested credential rotation. Avoid a generic repository abstraction, schema redesign, or role-per-table matrix.

## Acceptance Criteria

A threat model justifies the split; retained roles complete normal flows and are denied meaningful unrelated writes; migrations have a separate owner; rotation/rollback is tested; no speculative role matrix is added.
acceptance_criteria: A written threat model justifies the split; each retained runtime role completes normal flows and is denied at least one meaningful unrelated write; migrations use a separate owner; Compose/OpenShift secret rotation and rollback are tested; the shared role is removed only after a safe transition; no speculative role matrix is added.
close_reason: Separated migration ownership from runtime database authority

title: Strengthen typed JSON seams and behavior-focused quality checks
description:
Ruff currently enforces only basic E/F rules, tests are outside strict Pyright, and dynamic JSON/tool seams retain concentrated `Any` use. Some tests still couple to private helpers or exact mock arguments; one such assertion currently preserves failure-status comment ordering rather than public behavior. The internal GitHub gateway also repeats bounded-body parsing and exception ladders, but source review found no current semantic drift.

Improve one owned parser/test seam at a time. Replace private/mock wiring assertions with public behavior, add only green high-signal lint rules, and consider one gateway-local JSON-body decoder only if it removes duplication without coupling route-specific contracts. Do not add a generic HTTP client/framework, repository-wide type purge, or large test matrix.

## Acceptance Criteria

Selected JSON seams narrow values without broad ignores; lint expands only while green; public behavior replaces wiring assertions; any gateway consolidation stays local; no generic layer or broad purge is added.
acceptance_criteria: Selected external JSON seams narrow object values without broad ignores; lint expands only where green; public behavior tests replace private/mock-wiring coupling; any gateway consolidation is local and behavior-preserving; no generic HTTP layer, coverage threshold, type purge, or large matrix is added.

The false scan claim is removed first; any adopted gate covers Python, both npm locks, and exact image digests under one documented severity/exception policy; reports are retained and SBOM/provenance remain intact.

title: Exclude admission credentials from diagnostics
description:
`AdmissionConfig` uses the generated dataclass representation for `database_url` and `github_app_secret`. Both values are credentials, while sibling runtime/App configuration classes already mark equivalent fields `repr=False`. Any diagnostic, assertion failure, or future structured logging of this config can therefore disclose the PostgreSQL password and webhook HMAC secret.

Reuse the existing dataclass convention; do not add a redaction framework.

## Steps to Reproduce

Construct `AdmissionConfig` with sentinel credentials and call `repr`; both the database URL and webhook secret appear in the result.

## Acceptance Criteria

The representation contains neither credential; loading, comparison, readiness, and webhook behavior remain unchanged; a focused regression test protects both fields; no redaction framework is added.
acceptance_criteria: The representation of `AdmissionConfig` contains neither a sentinel database URL nor webhook secret; config loading, comparison, readiness, and webhook behavior remain unchanged; a focused regression test protects both fields; no generic secret wrapper or logging framework is added.
close_reason: Admission credentials are excluded from representations, responses, and raw failure diagnostics; fixed response and diagnostic contracts are behavior-tested.

title: Separate release evidence generation from write permissions
description:
The release evidence job runs pinned third-party Syft and Trivy actions while the
job also holds contents, attestation, artifact-metadata, and OIDC write
permissions. Pinning constrains upstream drift, but the token is still available
inside the job and the new scanner increases the privileged execution surface.

After the vulnerability gate is stable in real releases, split generation and
scanning from publication: a read-only job should generate inventories, scan the
exact platform digests, enforce policy, and upload one immutable workflow
artifact; a small write-authorized job should download that exact artifact,
attest it, and attach it to the matching release. Preserve exact tag/SHA/digest
binding and do not add a staging registry or generic release framework unless
promotion-before-publication becomes a separately approved requirement.

## Acceptance Criteria

Pinned third-party evidence and scanner actions run with only contents/package
read permissions; only the final attestation/release-attachment job has write
permissions; the handoff artifact is exact-source and checksum verified; failed
scans cannot reach the write-authorized job; existing SBOM, provenance, checksum,
prerelease, and exact-digest behavior remains covered by observable workflow
tests.
close_reason: Release evidence generation now runs read-only; the only write-authorized job verifies a closed file set, strict checksum coverage, exact source SHA, and published image digest before attestation and attachment.

title: Scan recent failure-status comments before publishing duplicates
description:
Failure-status recovery is the only publication comment scan that omits `newest_first=True`; its focused test currently asserts that omission. On a long pull request, the bounded scan can therefore inspect only the oldest comments, miss the agent's recent marker, and create a duplicate failure-status comment. The normal publication and review-comment scans already use newest-first ordering.

Reuse that established bounded scan convention. Do not add unbounded pagination or a generic provider scan abstraction.

## Steps to Reproduce

Create more old issue comments than the bounded scan window, place a recent Review Agent failure-status marker after them, and observe oldest-first recovery miss it.

## Acceptance Criteria

Failure-status scans are newest-first and bounded; recent markers are recovered without duplication; tests assert public recovery behavior rather than only mock wiring.
acceptance_criteria: Failure-status scans request newest-first ordering and remain bounded; recovery finds a recent canonical marker even when older comments exceed the page window; duplicate publication is prevented; tests assert public recovery behavior rather than only mock wiring.
close_reason: Recent failure markers are now recovered through supported bounded tail pagination.

No pagination framework or unbounded scan.

title: Make review-agent-memory failures secret-safe and inputs bounded
description:
`review-agent-memory` accepts several plain integer limits without finite upper bounds and sends expected as well as unexpected exceptions through a bare `_fatal(str(exception))` path. Common PostgreSQL and settings failures are already converted to secret-safe messages, so this is primarily an operator-input and diagnostic-quality gap, with preventive secret-safety value at remaining external seams.

Keep learning/coaching logic unchanged. Bound high-cost CLI inputs before opening resources, preserve structured domain failure semantics, and avoid collapsing programming errors into ambiguous bare messages. Reuse the stronger `review-agent-admin` adapter patterns only where they fit; do not introduce a generic CLI framework.

## Steps to Reproduce

Pass an extreme positive `--limit` or `--row-limit`, or raise an unexpected exception from a live command, and observe that parsing accepts the value and `_fatal` emits only its bare text.

## Acceptance Criteria

Excessive inputs fail before work; expected failures remain bounded and secret-safe; unexpected defects retain useful diagnostics without configured credentials; valid receipts remain compatible.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid, negative, or excessive high-cost limits fail before work; expected domain/runtime failures have bounded secret-safe output and stable exits; unexpected defects retain useful diagnostics without printing configured credentials; valid receipts remain compatible.
close_reason: Implemented bounded inputs and secret-safe operator failures

title: Define PostgreSQL retention and pruning ownership
description:
The repository already exercises PostgreSQL dump/restore against a fresh database and documents a basic operator recovery path. The remaining gap is retention ownership: durable reviews, webhook deliveries, publications, feedback, audit rows, and private coaching receipts can grow indefinitely without a table-by-table retention and pruning policy.

Define retention only for data with a clear legal and product owner. Add a bounded, observable, dependency-aware operator path where deletion is approved; preserve audit-relevant history by default. Do not add partitioning, a second archive service, or another database without measured need.

## Acceptance Criteria

Each table has a retention owner and exemption rule; approved pruning is bounded, observable, dry-run capable, FK-safe, and covered by the existing restore drill; no speculative partition/archive system is added.
acceptance_criteria: Table-by-table retention owners, exemptions, and default preservation rules are documented; any pruning command is bounded, observable, dry-run capable, FK-safe, and covered by the existing backup/restore drill; no partition framework or archive service is added without measurements.
close_reason: Implemented bounded, dry-run-first retention ownership

title: Own production upgrades and rollbacks by exact image digest
description:
Production deployment lacks one canonical upgrade and rollback runbook. Current examples use version tags, OpenShift applies zero-replica deployments and initialization jobs without an explicit wait for old replicas to terminate, and the expand-only rule for future migrations exists only in internal execution history. This can make image identity and migration ordering ambiguous during an upgrade.

Own the complete production sequence in `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`: select exact Review Agent and PostgreSQL image digests; drain and verify old application replicas before migration; run initialization jobs from the new digest; start and verify the new replicas; and roll back only to a database-compatible prior digest. State the expand-first rule for future incompatible schema changes. Do not rewrite immutable migrations 001-012 or build migration tooling until another violation proves it necessary. Extract any still-useful operational rules before archiving internal Goal Maker state.

## Acceptance Criteria

Production guidance uses exact digests; old replicas are observed stopped before migration; initialization/start/verification order is executable; rollback names its database compatibility boundary; future migrations are expand-first; immutable migrations remain unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Production Compose/Dokploy and OpenShift guidance uses exact application and database digests; old replicas are drained and observed stopped before migrations; initialization and new-replica verification order is executable; rollback names the compatible prior digest and database boundary; future migrations follow expand-first rules; immutable migrations are unchanged.
close_reason: Production upgrades now use exact image identities, fail-closed drain/migrate/start sequencing, and evidence-backed database-compatible rollback across Compose, Dokploy, and OpenShift.

title: Measure and bound large-PR and queue resource use
description:
Several scale costs are plausible but not yet measured: changed-file enumeration can repeat complete passes while retaining raw patches; source pagination rereads whole files; fair job claiming sorts by an aging expression not served by the current index; GitHub App intake is serial per process; publisher replicas may contend before fenced claims; and worker pools consume `concurrency + 1` database connections per replica.

Measure the existing owners before changing behavior. Include a representative multi-repository deployment so the result answers whether 100 repositories and concurrent reviews fit the queue, publisher, App intake, memory, and PostgreSQL connection budgets. Do not add caches, quotas, queue services, or indexes until the measurements identify a material bottleneck.

## Acceptance Criteria

Benchmarks cover a 3,000-file PR, 100/1,000/10,000 jobs, multiple publishers, App intake, and 100-repository concurrency; they record requests, latency, RSS, buffers/locks, and pool waiters; only measured bottlenecks are changed.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmarks cover a 3000-file PR, 100/1000/10000 queued jobs, 1/2/10 publisher replicas, GitHub App intake, and a representative 100-repository concurrency mix; results record requests, wall time, peak RSS, PostgreSQL buffers/locks, pool waiters, and queue latency; accepted changes preserve coverage, fairness, revisions, and bounds; speculative machinery is rejected.
close_reason: Measured the approved production-scale scenarios

title: Normalize repository identity in offline learning exports
description: Offline export and learning filters compared repository names case-sensitively even though GitHub identity and live PostgreSQL lookup are case-insensitive. Mixed-case --repo input could silently omit all matching rows, while the resulting output still appeared complete. Quality and coaching analysis could therefore diverge by letter casing or report success over the wrong repository scope.\n\nNormalize comparison and rendered identity at the existing offline export and learning owner. A complete export for a registered repository may legitimately contain no history; validity comes from complete=true plus an exact case-insensitive match with the export's declared top-level repository, not from a non-empty evidence table. Do not introduce a repository service or change durable identity.
acceptance_criteria: Case variants select the same canonical rows and provenance without cross-repository leakage and render identical learning and coaching identities; matching complete exports with no history remain valid; mismatched, missing, or malformed repository identity fails before analysis; focused export, learning, and coaching tests pass.
close_reason: Offline learning and coaching now use one case-insensitive repository identity without cross-repository leakage.

title: Make best-effort failure-persistence loss observable
description:
`review_tool_runtime.mark_run_failed` deliberately preserves the primary tool error when durable failure recording also fails, but it catches the persistence exception without any operator-visible log. The primary response remains correct while an important database/recovery failure becomes invisible.

Do not add an outbox or new recovery service unless evidence shows the current lease/run recovery cannot handle it.

## Steps to Reproduce

Make `fail_live_run` raise while a tool is handling its primary failure and observe no operator-visible record of the persistence failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

The secondary failure is logged with bounded, secret-safe run context; the original public error is preserved; current recovery is verified; no new service is added.
acceptance_criteria: A secondary failure while marking a run failed is logged with bounded run context and no secrets; the original tool failure remains the public result; existing recovery behavior is verified for the stranded run; no new queue, outbox, or service is introduced.
